changelog: Fixed candle spacing changing mid-replay (Next Bar, Prev Bar, and Play): bar spacing is now set once, as a real chart option, when a session opens/resumes/rewinds/switches display timeframe -- a plain Next Bar step only ever scrolls to the live edge, it never re-fits the view.

The trader can now pan/zoom the replay chart manually without it snapping back on the next step: doing so pauses auto-follow (same inference technique the price axis's own manual-scale detection already uses), and a new 'Jump to Latest' button (next to Prev Bar/Next Bar) resumes it -- reintroduces the button removed in v3.20.11, whose original 'every step re-centers anyway' reasoning no longer holds now that panning is possible.

Fixed a resize-ordering bug on session open/resume and display-timeframe switch where the chart's bar spacing could be computed against a stale container width, then the canvas resized afterward without re-fitting -- visible as the chart looking subtly stretched/cramped right after opening a session.

Play (auto-advance) no longer lets two steps overlap if a response is slow -- a second advance firing before the first one's own round trip finished could occasionally render an earlier window after a later one, visible as the chart briefly jumping backward mid-Play.

The plain (non-backtest) chart's own 'load older candles on scroll back' pagination no longer fires during an active backtest session, where it isn't aware of the replay's own fixed candle window and could silently grow/corrupt it.
release_notes: No DB migration. Investigated and confirmed already-correct (no change needed): drawing anchors (Fib retracement, rectangle/zone) are stored as {time, price} and converted to pixels fresh on every render via btTimeToX()/btPriceToY() -- never pixels, never clamped to the canvas when off-screen; future candles are never in the dataset passed to the chart (BacktestController::getCandles()'s own replay_cursor_ms clamp, server-side, confirmed independent of this fix); the price axis's autoscaleInfoProvider already derives its natural range from Lightweight Charts' own visible-bars computation. The root cause was narrower than 'candle width drifts during normal Play' (a direct 30-bar Next Bar probe against the pre-fix code showed bar spacing already numerically stable there) -- it was that the per-step setVisibleLogicalRange() call had no notion of a trader having manually zoomed/panned, so the very next step yanked the view straight back to the fixed window, which is what actually reads as 'stretching.' Fixed spacing is now a real timeScale option (barSpacing/rightOffset) applied once per fresh load; every step only calls scrollToPosition() (a pure scroll, confirmed via Lightweight Charts' own scrollPosition()/logicalToCoordinate() API that it does not touch bar spacing), gated behind a new btAutoFollow flag tracked via subscribeVisibleLogicalRangeChange(). Verified via tools/ui-harness: every pre-existing driver (drive.mjs through drive-v3250.mjs, 11 total) passes unmodified after this change, plus three new throwaway probes run during development (not committed as permanent drivers) confirming (1) bar spacing is bit-for-bit identical across 30 Next Bar steps, (2) a manual pan freezes the view exactly through a subsequent step with auto-follow correctly reporting paused, and (3) Jump to Latest resumes auto-follow and the next step auto-scrolls again. php -l and node --check clean on every changed file; duplicate-name scan clean. Not yet verified from this environment: a real mouse-driven pan/zoom in an actual browser (the probes drove the Lightweight Charts API directly, not real pointer events) and the full acceptance scenario (BTCUSDT 1H at Apr 08 18:00, Play at 1x for 30 bars) against live data.
